transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

To be honest, I'm a bit embarrassed to be here, but I've been having a hard time since I transitioned off my long-haul driving routes. I keep eating in the evenings until I’m so full it’s uncomfortable, even when I don’t really want more.

When these evening overeating episodes happen, do you feel like you cannot stop or control how much you eat, and do you ever try to make up for it afterward by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or excessive exercise?

Yes, it feels like something takes over and I'm just watching myself grab one thing after another, even while I'm telling myself to stop. I don't do anything to try and make up for it afterward like throwing up or fasting—I just sit there in the quiet feeling gross and ashamed of myself.
Do these eating episodes happen at least once a week for the past 3 months, or are they less frequent than that?

Yes, they happen much more than once a week—it's pretty much every night, or at least several times a week. It's been going on for about three months now, starting around when my divorce was finalized and I transitioned to this new office role.
Do you feel very distressed or upset by these eating episodes, and have you noticed any significant weight changes since they started?

I feel deeply ashamed and beat myself up every time it happens, and it's gotten to the point where I avoid going out with my buddies because I'm so embarrassed. As for my weight, I'm not really sure if there's been a big change since I haven't weighed myself lately.
Have you ever intentionally tried to lose weight by restricting food, following strict dieting rules, or exercising a lot because of your eating episodes?

No, I haven't really tried restricting my food or following any strict diets to make up for it. I also don't do any excessive exercising after those nights. I usually just feel too sluggish and ashamed the next morning to even think about trying that.
Have you ever had a period where you were intentionally trying to lose weight or control your shape with strict dieting, fasting, vomiting, laxatives, or excessive exercise?

No, I've never tried any of those methods to control my weight or shape. I've never been one for strict dieting, fasting, or using things like laxatives and vomiting. It's just not something I've ever done.
Have you ever had times when you deliberately tried to lose weight or control your shape by strict dieting, fasting, vomiting, laxatives, or excessive exercise?
No, I've never tried any of those things to control my shape or weight. I've never been one for strict dieting, fasting, or anything like that.
Have you ever had a time when you intentionally tried to lose weight or control your shape by strict dieting, fasting, vomiting, laxatives, or excessive exercise?
No, I've never really tried any of those methods like strict dieting, fasting, or extreme exercising to control my weight or shape. It's just not something I have ever done.
How much do your weight and body shape affect how you feel about yourself? For example, do they strongly influence your self-esteem or the way you judge yourself?

I haven't really thought about my weight or shape being the main issue. For me, the shame and self-judgment are mostly about my inability to control my eating behavior and how I can't seem to stop myself in those moments.
Do your weight or body shape strongly affect how you judge your self-worth, or is the main problem the loss of control and shame around the eating itself?

It's definitely the loss of control and the shame around the eating itself, rather than how I look or what I weigh. It is incredibly frustrating to feel like a passenger just watching myself eat without being able to stop. I just end up beating myself up afterward for having absolutely no self-control.
Have you ever been very focused on your weight or body shape, or felt that they strongly affect your self-esteem? Or is the main issue mainly the loss of control and shame about the eating itself?

The main issue is absolutely the loss of control and the shame of the eating itself, not how I look or what I weigh. I just feel so gross and embarrassed afterward, beating myself up because a grown man should be able to control what he puts in his own mouth.
Do you spend a lot of time worried about your weight or body shape, or is the main problem mainly the binge eating and feeling out of control?

The main problem is definitely the eating itself and feeling completely out of control. I don't really spend time worrying about my weight or shape, but I'm deeply ashamed that I can't seem to stop myself once I get started in the kitchen.
Have you ever been preoccupied with your weight, body shape, or fear of gaining weight, even if you do not act on it?
To be honest, I haven't really thought much about or been preoccupied with my weight or body shape. That just hasn't been my main focus at all.
Have you ever been significantly preoccupied with your weight, body shape, or fear of gaining weight, even if you did not try to lose weight in unhealthy ways?

No, I haven't ever really been preoccupied with my weight or how my body looks. My main concern is just the complete lack of control I have during those evening eating spells and the deep shame I feel afterward.
Did these binge-eating episodes start before age 18, or did they only begin in adulthood?

No, this is a completely new issue that only started about three months ago, well into my adulthood at age 59. I never experienced anything like this when I was younger or before age 18. It all began just recently after my divorce and transitioning off the road.
Have these binge-eating episodes been happening for at least 6 months, or have they only been present for about 3 months so far?

They have only been going on for about three months so far. They really just started around the time my divorce was finalized and I transitioned from long-haul driving to my new office and mentoring role.
Have you had any other eating problems before these past 3 months, such as episodes of overeating, severe dieting, purging, or a long-standing concern about weight or body shape?
No, I've never had any issues like this before these last three months. I never did any strict dieting, purging, or overeating in the past—it's all a very recent development for me.
